screens.heading: You are safe here
screens.reassurance: This module will not take any photos or access your camera. You are just reading.
screens.goal: By the end of this module, you will know how to take better photos, organise your photo library, create digital art, and share your memories with the people you love.

screens.heading: Betty's story
body: Betty, 78, had always loved painting watercolours. When arthritis made it harder to hold a brush, she thought her painting days were over. Then her granddaughter showed her a drawing app on the iPad.

'At first I thought it was silly — painting with your finger on a piece of glass,' Betty laughs. 'But then I discovered you could choose any colour instantly, undo a mistake with one tap, and zoom in to add tiny details.'
Betty now paints every evening after dinner and emails her work to friends as greeting cards. 'This little device gave me my art back,' she says.
screens.tellMeMore: You do not need any artistic experience to enjoy creative apps on your iPad or Android tablet. The most important thing is that mistakes are completely reversible — one tap on 'Undo' takes you back. There is no wasted paint, no ruined canvas, no mess to clean up.

screens.heading: Taking better photos
body: Open the Camera app on your device. Point it at what you want to photograph and tap the large round white button to take the picture.

For better photos: make sure your subject has good light (facing a window is ideal), hold the camera steady, and tap on the person's face on the screen before taking the photo — this tells the camera to focus there.
Your photos are automatically saved to your Photos app. You cannot accidentally delete the phone by taking too many pictures.
screens.tellMeMore: Portrait mode (available on newer iPhones and iPads) blurs the background and makes your subject stand out beautifully — great for photos of grandchildren. Look for the 'Portrait' option at the bottom of the Camera app. Also: the zoom is digital on most phones, which reduces quality. It is often better to walk a bit closer than to zoom in.

screens.heading: Organising your photos
body: Open the Photos app to see all your photos arranged by date. You can scroll back through years of memories in seconds.

To create an album: tap the Albums tab, then the + button, name your album (e.g., 'Grandkids 2026'), and select the photos to include. Albums do not move or delete photos — they are just a way to organise them.
To find a specific photo quickly: use the Search tab in the Photos app. Type 'beach,' 'birthday,' or a person's name (if you have tagged people) and your iPad will find matching photos automatically.
screens.tellMeMore: iCloud Photos (on Apple devices) can automatically back up all your photos to the cloud — so if your iPad is lost, stolen, or damaged, your photos are safe. Go to Settings → your name → iCloud → Photos → turn on iCloud Photos. You get 5 GB free. If you have many years of photos, you may need to pay for more storage (99 cents/month for 50 GB is the most popular option).

screens.heading: Creating art and sharing memories
body: For digital art: the app Procreate Pocket (iPhone/iPad, small one-time cost) is popular and powerful. Free alternatives include Adobe Fresco and Sketchbook. All let you paint, draw, and create with your finger or a stylus.

For greeting cards and photo books: the app Canva (free) lets you create beautiful cards using your own photos. Chatbooks and Artifact Uprising can print your photos into physical books — a wonderful gift for family.
To share a photo: open the photo, tap the Share button (a box with an arrow pointing up), and choose how to send it — text message, email, or a shared album.
screens.tellMeMore: Shared albums are one of the best family features on Apple devices. You create an album, invite family members to join, and everyone can add photos. Your grandchildren add their school photos; you add yours; everyone sees everyone else's. Set one up by opening the Photos app, tapping the + under Shared Albums, naming it, and entering your family members' email addresses.

screens.heading: Your device is a camera, studio, and memory keeper
takeaways: Tap on a face before taking a photo — the camera focuses there and the results are much better.
Create Albums to organise your photos — albums are just labels, they do not move or delete the originals.
iCloud Photos backs up every photo automatically — your memories are safe even if your device is lost.
Procreate Pocket and Canva are great starting points for digital art and greeting cards.
The Share button (box with arrow) lets you send any photo by text, email, or shared album.
screens.confidence: You now know how to take beautiful photos, keep them organised, create digital art, and share your memories with everyone who matters.
